newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-NAGANO GAMES PROMISES MONKEYS AMONG FIRSTS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NAGANO GAMES PROMISES MONKEYS AMONG FIRSTS.

text.p: The 1998 Nagano Winter Games are the Olympic movement's farewell to the 20th century and plan to go out in style with a host of firsts -- including monkeys.
With competition scheduled in a record 68 events in 11 sports, Nagano will be the biggest Winter Games ever.
That is only the start of Nagano's record-breaking plans.
How about the first games to have an official sake, pickles and soba noodles?

Still not impressed? Then what about the glory of sinking your teeth into the Olympic movement's first official apple? Local farmers have embedded skins of young apples with the Nagano's snowflower emblem.
Then there is the first appearance by a "Dream Team" at a Winter Olympics.

Ice hockey professionals from North America's National Hockey League (NHL) will make their first Olympic appearance in Nagano for Canada and the United States following the example of the U.S. basketball "Dream Team" in the 1992 summer games.
Biathlon is already in the environmental record book as the first Olympic sport to cede its venue to native wildlife.
The biathlon course has been moved to Nozawa Onsen, 50 km (30 miles) north-east of Nagano, to protect rare goshawks and buzzards found nesting at the intended site in Hakuba.
Ski jumpers may be in for a double first in 1998 because of winds which whip through the hills where they jump.
Arrangements already have been made to mount a prototype windscreen to protect jumpers from crosswinds.

Three synthetic nets set up on cranes for a World Cup competition last month gave no protection because the winds were head rather than crosswinds so organisers are now considering installing floodlights in case the events need to be held at night when the winds die down.
Luge and bobsleigh athletes will compete on the first track in the world to have two uphill sections, needed say organisers to minimise changes to the slope.
The village of Karuizawa goes into Summer and Winter Games record books as the first site to stage events for both games.
Equestrian events were held at the resort town, 90 km (55 miles) southeast of Nagano, in the 1964 Tokyo Summer Olympics.
Karuizawa this time hosts the debut of curling as an Olympic sport. Snowboarding and women's ice hockey also make their debuts at Nagano.

And the monkeys? Snowboard competitors at Kanbayashi, 40 km (25 miles) north-east of Nagano, will vie for the attention of spectators with a nearby park's famous wild monkeys, who often sit in thermal pools to keep warm.
